newsitem.title: USA: Seagate reports weak Q4 results.
newsitem.headline: Seagate reports weak Q4 results.

text.p: Seagate Technology Inc. Wednesday reported weak fourth-quarter profits, reflecting lower demand for high-end disk drives.

The company reported earnings of $59.3 million, or 23 cents a share, on revenues of $1.98 billion for its fourth quarter, ended June 27. In the comparable year-ago quarter, Seagate had profits of $101 million, or 46 cents a share, on revenues of $2.0 billion.
Excluding $155.5 million in one-time charges, fully diluted earnings per share for the latest quarter were 61 cents, compared with 52 cents a year earlier, without charges.

Seagate, the world's biggest computer disk drive maker, had warned investors twice in June that its fourth-quarter earnings would be worse than previously expected due to weak demand for high-end disk drives and some internal production issues.

Analysts had expected the Scotts Valley, Calif.-based company to record earnings of 66 cents a share, excluding charges, according to First Call, which monitors Wall Street earnings forecasts. At the start of June, before Seagate warned that its profits would be weak, the consensus estimate had been $1.06 a share.

The company said in a statement that it expects to record a pre-tax charge from currency hedging of about $25 million in its upcoming first quarter as a result of the recent devaluation of the Thai Baht. That charge should be more than offset by the benefits of recording local currency expenses in lower U.S. dollar terms, the company said.
Seagate had profits for the 1997 fiscal year of $658 million, or $2.73 a share, on revenues of $8.94 billion. A year earlier it earned $213.2 million, or $1.03 a share, on revenues of $8.6 billion.
Seagate's stock closed up $1.125 at $38.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
